races.name: Morgan's Army Fighting Spirit Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rhodes Runner
runners_data.note: A front-runner with 4/5 runs on similar Good ground and genuine pace, Rossa Ryan takes over for Ralph Beckett who is in decent 14-day form (5/35); has finished placed on Good ground before but has not won in five tries and faces a direct rival for the lead in Downonmainstreet.
runners_data.comment: Twice placed in her last five starts — second three starts back and third four starts back — Rhodes Runner arrives here 19 days fresh, with experience over today's trip and a rating nudging above her official mark; yet to score, and carrying 135 lb from stall six is the one factor to weigh.

runners_data.name: Wild Terrain
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's gelding won on Good ground over this trip but has returned form figures of 0-0-0 since, and carries a hood; Daniel Muscutt picks up the ride but the fade-in-finish flag is a serious concern over a flat 6f against pace rivals who will not slow down.
runners_data.comment: Wild Terrain won four starts back but has been unplaced in his three subsequent runs, and his trainer is in poor nick at just 2/37 over the past fortnight; he has run over today's trip and going, and our rating has him fifth of seven.

runners_data.name: Downonmainstreet
runners_data.note: David Egan partners this Michael Bell-trained filly who arrives off a 5f win on Good ground; she is a natural front-runner stepping up to 6f for the first time, and if she can handle the extra furlong she has the freshest winning form in the field, though trainer's 14-day strike-rate of 1/19 is modest.
runners_data.comment: Downonmainstreet catches the eye on the back of a win last time out, and she has run over today's trip before, so conditions pose no surprises; a seventh three starts back is forgiven, and at 21 days between runs she arrives here in fine order.

runners_data.name: Tango Hotel
runners_data.note: George Scott's colt wears a hood and has consecutive placed efforts over 6f on Good ground, making him ideally profiled as a prominent runner who can track the pace duel; Liam Wright (3) claims 3lb and the 41-day absence is worth monitoring, but the form profile suits this scenario well.
runners_data.comment: Tango Hotel shaped with clear promise when runner-up last time out and two starts back, and that winning effort three starts back underlines her quality; experience over today's trip and going is a further asset, though 41 days off the track is the one question mark she must answer.

runners_data.name: Laylaty
runners_data.note: Harry Charlton's filly won over 6f on Good ground last time out and sits neatly in the prominent bracket; Lewis Edmunds is a low-profile booking but the horse's own form — 1-3-4 in reverse — shows genuine ability on this surface and trip.
runners_data.comment: Ranked toward the foot of the assessments on these figures, Laylaty faces a stiff ask, though she does arrive on the back of a win last time out, has run over today's trip, and a 26-day absence suggests she returns fresh.

runners_data.name: Minzaal Time
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes's runner has all five career runs over 7f on Standard or Good ground, making this step down to 6f on Turf a significant style change; the best going figure is 5th on Stalls, form reads 0-7-8-5 in recent outings, and there is little evidence to suggest a market move is coming.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Minzaal Time faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip before and returns on a relatively fresh 22 days; the 129 lb burden does him no favours either.

runners_data.name: Seed Ya Later
runners_data.note: Jack Channon's horse returns just 10 days after its last run and has broad experience over 5-6f on Good ground; Kieran Shoemark is a strong booking and the horse has shown versatility in its form string, but the recent rhythm of finishing mid-to-rear in most runs makes it more of an each-way type than a winner in this shape.
runners_data.comment: Seed Ya Later rates as the one to beat on our figures, and her third two starts back hints at a return to form — the main risk is finding her best after a seventh three starts back interrupted that progression.

races.paceDynamic: Rhodes Runner and Downonmainstreet are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off on this straight 6f Ffos Las track, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft, uncontested lead for either. Rhodes Runner has recent Good-ground course experience and will press hard, while Downonmainstreet arrives off a win over 5f and may find the extra furlong stretching stamina if the pace burns hot early. Tango Hotel, Laylaty, and Seed Ya Later are prominent types who will press just off the duel, meaning the first three or four positions will be densely populated through the early stages. This race shape — a genuine pace duel up front with prominent runners tracking just behind — classically favours horses who can sit just off a hot pace and finish through the line, making the prominent-to-midfield profile that can sustain momentum the prime tactical beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Duel, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Rhodes Runner and Downonmainstreet fight each other genuinely and a prominent tracker collects.
scenarios.body: The front two burn each other off through the first three furlongs, leaving one of the pressing prominent types — Tango Hotel or Laylaty — to sweep past on fumes; on Good ground over 6f at Ffos Las this is the textbook outcome for a two-runner pace duel with handy types directly behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If one front-runner asserts quickly and the other fades, leaving a controlled solo lead.
scenarios.body: Downonmainstreet, with the most recent winning form, could establish a clear lead by the halfway point if Rhodes Runner fails to sustain the duel, giving Michael Bell's runner a soft lead that rewards her pace-forcing style; a controlled 6f on Good ground suits a horse stepping up from winning over 5f if the gallop is not excessive.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Flier Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly scorching and the hold-up horses receive a strong tailwind of pace to close into.
scenarios.body: Wild Terrain and Minzaal Time would need the front two to go suicidally fast to get into this over a flat 6f, and Wild Terrain's recent form shows a pattern of fading finishes that undercuts confidence; only a genuinely extreme pace meltdown makes this viable and that is not guaranteed given both front-runners are rated close together.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If neither front-runner is able to stride clear and the whole field bunches entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A chaotic flat finish over 6f at Ffos Las would be unusual on Good ground with two genuine pace types, but a complete collapse in order would open the race to any of the prominent runners with a late burst; Seed Ya Later's course experience and Laylaty's recent winning form give them the best residual claims in a scramble.

watchPoints.text: Rhodes Runner and Downonmainstreet — watch the first furlong closely; if one blinks and concedes the lead, the pace dynamic shifts from a duel to a solo front-runner scenario and the race shape changes completely.

Tango Hotel — 41 days off the track is the longest absence in the field and the hood suggests some temperament management; watch at the stalls and in the first furlong to see if the freshness is an asset or a problem.

Wild Terrain — despite the win on Good ground, three consecutive zeros since suggests something is wrong; if it begins to fade before the two-furlong pole it confirms the fade-in-finish flag and removes it as a threat entirely.

Laylaty — if Edmunds gets her away cleanly and she settles just off the pace duel by lengths one or two, she is ideally positioned in the most favoured scenario; a rough break or early traffic would cost her the position she needs.

Minzaal Time — the trip drop from 7f to 6f is untested and Finley Marsh has limited race-reading options on a flat straight track; watch whether it is withdrawn if any significant market drift appears pre-race as a signal the stable has concerns.

races.name: Shirgar Welsh Butter Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Channel Islands
runners_data.note: David Evans handler in fair form (2 wins from 16 runners in 14 days), but this runner posted a modest fifth over 7f on Good — dropping to 6f may suit, though racing out of a slightly pushed-up position means it must deliver at the front or the rating advantage is undermined.

runners_data.name: Corbie Rock
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam sends out a debutant with Rhys Clutterbuck aboard and no public form to assess; the unknown style tag means race positioning is a complete unknown, and backers are betting entirely on trainer reputation and home reputation.

runners_data.name: Native Chief
runners_data.note: John Butler's runner has a recent start over 7f on Standard (Southwell) and carries a concerning fade-in-finish flag; David Egan is a strong booking but the hold-up style on a track that doesn't always reward late runs from out of the gate is a tactical ask.

runners_data.name: Tumishi
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's juvenile has two placed efforts over 6f on Good ground (3rd and 4th), giving it directly relevant course-distance-going form — its natural style is prominent, but the crowded pace map in this race means it is liable to be pushed back from where it wants to race, which is an inconvenient complication for an otherwise straightforward profile.

runners_data.name: War Gaming
runners_data.note: George Scott's consistent type brings three efforts all on Good ground over 5-6f (2-3-3), making it the most proven horse in the field for conditions; Rossa Ryan takes the ride, headgear is noted (p), and its prominent style fits the anticipated race shape naturally — this runner looks best positioned to fill the key slot just off the leader.

runners_data.name: Duchess Of Immatin
runners_data.note: George Boughey sends out another debutant, this time with Kieran Shoemark — a top-level booking — which hints at stable confidence; 128lbs is the lightest weight in the field, and with style and ability both unknown, the Shoemark appointment is the primary reason to include it in any tactical calculus.

races.paceDynamic: Channel Islands is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to contest the lead, should be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 6f on Good turf at Ffos Las. War Gaming and Tumishi carry prominent profiles but, with Channel Islands likely to stride into the lead uncontested, at least one of those types will be unable to fulfil their natural role and will be pushed wider in the order than ideal. This creates a steady-to-moderate pace scenario rather than a true end-to-end gallop, which typically rewards horses who can travel close to the action and produce a clean, sustained finish rather than those who need a fast early tempo to set up a late run. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate — Channel Islands is best placed to secure the rail and the lead, with War Gaming most likely to take up a prominent slot just behind, while Tumishi is the type most likely to find themselves shuffled into a position further back than their natural style demands. This race shape most favours prominent-to-lead profiles who can control the fractions and sustain their effort to the line on a flat, fair track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Channel Islands takes an uncontested lead and dictates a fair-to-steady gallop that suits its prominent profile.
scenarios.body: Channel Islands bowls along at the front, sets a manageable tempo, and the race is run at a pace that rewards those closest to the action rather than late challengers; any horse that travels fluently in second or third is ideally positioned for a sustained run to the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If War Gaming pushes up to challenge Channel Islands for the lead, creating a genuine two-horse tussle from the front.
scenarios.body: An early duel between Channel Islands and War Gaming raises the tempo slightly, making the race more of a test of stamina and courage for those who commit early; a horse just off the pace travelling smoothly could capitalise if both front-runners give each other too much to do.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong and a closer gets a clear run through.
scenarios.body: Native Chief, despite a concerning finishing tendency and a wide draw concern, could benefit if a genuine injection of pace in the first half sets up a late dash; this shape is unlikely given the moderate tempo anticipated, but a fading front-runner opens the door for anything with residual stamina.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Upsets The Market
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two lightly-raced, unraced runners — Corbie Rock or Duchess Of Immatin — shows unexposed talent to overhaul the field.
scenarios.body: Both Corbie Rock (Jane Chapple-Hyam) and Duchess Of Immatin (George Boughey, Kieran Shoemark) arrive without a public form line, leaving their true ability unknown; if either holds a significant raw ability advantage the race shape becomes secondary, though this scenario depends entirely on hidden quality outweighing tactical disadvantage.

watchPoints.text: War Gaming carries the headgear flag (p) and has a consistent placed record on Good ground at this trip — watch whether Rossa Ryan pushes for the lead early or settles just behind Channel Islands, as that decision shapes the entire race.

Tumishi cannot get its preferred prominent position if Channel Islands and War Gaming both assert — watch the early stages to see if Daniel Muscutt commits forward or accepts a midfield berth, as the latter would significantly alter its prospects.

Native Chief has a fade-in-finish concern flagged — watch whether David Egan opts to push it closer than its natural hold-up style to compensate, as doing so against a steady pace risks exposing that weakness even earlier.

Both Corbie Rock and Duchess Of Immatin are debutants with no public form — watch the market moves close to post time, as any significant move for either would be the only meaningful pre-race signal available.

Channel Islands was last seen 47 days ago and finished fifth over 7f — watch its early stride pattern to judge whether it is sharp enough to stride into the lead comfortably or whether it idles in front, which would invite War Gaming to assert.

races.name: Cjch Solicitors Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Coast
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Scott Dixon who has placed twice in similar going but is seven years old and faces the challenge of a cramped midfield rather than its preferred trailing berth; Kieran O'Neill takes over and will need a gap to open late from OR 44.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked seventh of nine on our figures, Coast faces a stiff task, though she has run over today's trip and going before and her third three starts back offers a crumb of form; a trainer striking at just 5% over the past fortnight does her no favours.

runners_data.name: Diamondsinthesand
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old whose recent form figures of 777686 suggest a horse looking for a kinder opportunity; apprentice Taryn Langley (5lb claim) is a potential leveller, but the horse's best form comes on softer surfaces and six Good-ground runs in this sample return only one win and two places.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of nine on ratings despite an official mark of just 46, Diamondsinthesand has distance and going experience to call upon and arrives fresh on 30 days' rest, yet the stark risk is a winless recent run of six starts that offers no obvious upturn in form to pin hopes on.

runners_data.name: Macarone
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan is a strong booking for Grace Harris and this five-year-old showed a second place over 6f on Good just 18 days ago, giving it the most directly relevant recent form in the field; races from a hold-up position but the form reads as a genuine closer rather than a shuffled-back runner.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Macarone does at least bring experience of today's distance and going, and a second two starts back shows he can threaten, though finishes of fifth on either side of it highlight the inconsistency that keeps him mid-division at a mark of 47.

runners_data.name: Outer Edge
runners_data.note: Christopher Mason's five-year-old has been quietly consistent with four placings from six Good-ground runs and returns after 42 days off; Gina Mangan partners and the horse's style is a genuine hold-up type, so it will need the field to fan out and create room in the straight to repeat those placed efforts.
runners_data.comment: Outer Edge has run over today's trip and going and his rating of 53 edges above his official mark, suggesting he holds claims here; the worry is that he has been winless in his last five starts, with a string of fourth and fifth-place finishes.

runners_data.name: Sundiata Keita
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in this race and therefore the key pace-shaping force; Taylor Fisher for John & Rhys Flint and the horse has placed twice on Good ground including a second over 5f last time, so the step to 6f is a question mark, though its tactical advantage of setting an uncontested tempo is significant with only 10 days' rest.
runners_data.comment: Sundiata Keita shaped with clear promise when second three starts back, and he has run over today's trip and going, returning fit on just ten days' rest from stall three carrying 135 lb; the concern is he has been winless in recent starts and was unplaced last time.

runners_data.name: Demetris Mouflon
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's three-year-old was last seen finishing second over 7f on Good 80 days ago and has now come back to 6f; Lewis Edmunds rides and the horse's natural instinct to settle off the pace means it finds itself pushed into a competitive midfield rather than enjoying clear air at the back — the layoff is worth monitoring.
runners_data.comment: Second last time out and carrying 55 on our ratings as the top-ranked runner of nine, Demetris Mouflon has run over today's trip and going before and arrives fresh after 80 days off; yet to win in her last five starts, but that recent runner-up shows the spark is there.

runners_data.name: Mayflower Rock
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha has been in good form (5/21 over 14 days) and David Egan is an upgrade in the saddle; the three-year-old's recent third over 5f on Good shows it handles the conditions and it has course form over 6f, though its placed efforts have come when getting a clear run rather than from a traffic-laden midfield.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Mayflower Rock faces a stiff task, though a third two starts back offers faint encouragement and she has run over today's trip before.

runners_data.name: Ridger
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster's three-year-old has struggled to convert, finishing in the top half just once across four starts with a form string of 6997; tongue tie applied and Stevie Donohoe takes the ride, but only one of four runs has come on Good ground and none of those efforts suggest the horse is capable of winning from its compressed map position.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked last on our figures, Ridger faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and returns after 14 days, but a sequence of sevenths and nineths makes him hard to fancy at 132 lb from stall five.

runners_data.name: Rogue Rebellion
runners_data.note: R Harris has no runners in the 14-day window to judge stable form, but Daniel Muscutt's appointment is a positive; the three-year-old has placed twice on Good ground from eight efforts over 6f and its recent consistency (3-4-3-4-5) suggests it finds its level without quite winning — a natural hold-up type squeezed into midfield rather than given room to settle and wind up.
runners_data.comment: Rogue Rebellion has been knocking on the door without a win, posting a third three starts back, though he has struggled to convert and comes into this off an 18-day break carrying 132 lb from stall one, with experience over today's trip and going at least offering some encouragement.

races.paceDynamic: Sundiata Keita is the sole confirmed front-runner in a nine-runner field and should stride into an uncontested lead from the outset over this 6f Ffos Las track on Good ground, setting a sustainable, controlled tempo rather than a pressured gallop. The remainder of the field is largely composed of hold-up types — Coast, Diamondsinthesand, Macarone, Outer Edge, Demetris Mouflon, Ridger, Rogue Rebellion, and Mayflower Rock — meaning Sundiata Keita will face no genuine early challenge and can dictate every yard of the race. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear, with Demetris Mouflon, Rogue Rebellion, and Ridger among those unlikely to secure their natural trailing position and instead occupying a contested midfield. A lone, uncontested pace-setter on Good ground over 6f creates a race shape that strongly favours horses with the tactical speed to track the leader in second or third — with virtually no true prominent horse to press Sundiata Keita, any runner who can bridge the gap from midfield in the final furlong becomes the primary threat, though the steady tempo may see the front-runner last home.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sundiata Keita Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sundiata Keita settles uncontested on the front end and the hold-up pack fails to close on a sound surface.
scenarios.body: Sundiata Keita dictates a measured, confidence-boosting gallop and simply has too much in reserve for closers who must cover extra ground from an over-crowded midfield; the Good ground and 6f distance suits a horse that ran second over 5f on Good recently and steps up slightly in trip.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace is just slow enough to compress the field and one of the genuine hold-up types produces a strong late run.
scenarios.body: With so many horses travelling in a bunched midfield, any slight traffic clearance in the final 2f could allow the strongest finisher to pick off a front-runner who set little genuine pace; Macarone (2nd recently on Good over 6f) and Rogue Rebellion (consistent form figures on Good) hold the best finishing profiles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Traffic Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the over-populated midfield creates interference in the straight and one horse finds clear air earliest.
scenarios.body: With multiple redistributed hold-up types forced into a compressed mid-division, crowding through the final 2f is a genuine risk; the horse that gets a clean run soonest — likely Outer Edge or Mayflower Rock on their consistent placed form — benefits most.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Field Swamps
scenarios.trigger: If Sundiata Keita goes too fast for the conditions and ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: An overly ambitious early gallop on Good ground could see Sundiata Keita fade sharply, handing the race to whichever hold-up type has tracked closest; Demetris Mouflon (second over 7f on Good) and Macarone both have form to exploit a weakening leader.

watchPoints.text: Sundiata Keita has the entire race in its own hands — if Taylor Fisher controls the tempo sensibly, this horse is the primary danger to all, and punters should watch whether anything attempts to press it early in the first furlong.

The over-populated midfield — featuring Demetris Mouflon, Rogue Rebellion, Ridger and Coast all competing for the same real estate — creates a genuine traffic risk entering the final 2f; any horse drawn wide and forced to switch may lose critical momentum.

Macarone's recent second over 6f on Good (18 days ago) stands out as the most live piece of form, and Rossa Ryan will be looking to track Sundiata Keita from a closer position than the map implies — watch whether it travels smoothly in the early stages.

Demetris Mouflon returns from an 80-day break having previously shown its best form over 7f; the drop to 6f and the absence makes it a watch rather than a confident selection, but Rod Millman horses have been placed recently and Lewis Edmunds is experienced enough to manage the situation.

Outer Edge's 42-day absence and a lack of recent winning form (four runs without a win since OR 48) makes it one to monitor on ground it handles, particularly if it gets a clean passage — its recent placed consistency means it should not be dismissed if the race unfolds with a late rush.

races.name: Roly Poly Events Race Of Hope Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Good Onya Mate
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with Bell/Shoemark combination, 13 days fresh, has placed in similar Good-ground handicaps at this trip but recent form shows a fade to 4th and a 9th, and the congested rear-of-field scenario in this shape makes a clean run uncertain.
runners_data.comment: Good Onya Mate has shown glimpses of ability, finishing second three starts back, but has been winless in his last five and an unplaced effort two starts back tempers optimism; the 142 lb burden is a further ask, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Golden Flame
runners_data.note: 8-year-old hold-up type with proven winning form on Good going over 16f (1W5P in similar conditions), Lewis claiming 7lbs, and 35 days between runs could mean peak freshness; this is a horse that genuinely stays and whose Good-ground record is the best in the field.
runners_data.comment: Golden Flame arrives here in fine fettle, placed in each of his last three starts with a win three starts back, and he has experience of both today's trip and the going. The main risk is the 142 lb he carries.

runners_data.name: Lusaka
runners_data.note: Hold-up stayer with a solid placing record on Good ground (2W4P in similar conditions), fitted with a hood, 49 days since last run which is the longest absence in the field, and while consistent at this level the extended break adds a note of caution around match-sharpness.
runners_data.comment: Lusaka rates as the one to beat on our figures, and his consistency shines through — third last time out and a second four starts back make him a strong threat at this level despite carrying 142 lb; the main risk is that he has yet to score in his last six starts.

runners_data.name: Merrijig
runners_data.note: Strong recent form (1-6323 over 16-18f on Good) and a genuine hold-up stayer, but true running style places this horse at the back of the field in a race where most rivals share the same tactic — holds up well on Good ground (0W4P) and the STYLE_FIT score reflects difficulty getting a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Merrijig has been in fine fettle of late, finishing third last time out and a winner five starts back, with consistent placing in between; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, and after 41 days off, there is plenty to work with off 140 lb.

runners_data.name: Sneaky Blinder
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race, OR 57, Rossa Ryan aboard, 9 days since last run, and Good-going record is thin (0W1P from 2 runs) — the structural advantage is enormous given an uncontested lead, but the slim similar-going profile is worth noting against proven stayers.
runners_data.comment: Sneaky Blinder showed grit when second last time out and third two starts back, but a seventh three starts back tempers expectations; he has run over today's trip and going, and at 134 lb off an official mark of 57, the weight is no help.

runners_data.name: Beaune
runners_data.note: 4-year-old horse whose best form has come on Standard surfaces rather than Good turf, headgear noted (hood), and while consistent in placing (0W1P on Good) the style redistribution means this runner will race further back than ideal and must produce a strong finish from a compromised position.

runners_data.name: Simiyann
runners_data.note: Ian Williams in good 14-day form (3/30), 16 days since last run, tongue-tie and visor headgear combination, and solid Good-ground record (1W4P over 14-18f); genuinely stays this trip but, like several rivals, finds natural position at the rear unavailable and must produce from a middle-pack berth.
runners_data.comment: Simiyann has been consistently placed in his last three starts — third last time out, third and second in the two before that — and has run over today's trip and going, with our rating of 64 suggesting he merits respect; the concern is he remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Last Flight
runners_data.note: 3-year-old with lowest weight (120lbs) and no winning or placing form on Good going (0W0P from 1 run), most recent form on Standard, and stepping up sharply in trip context from earlier runs — true hold-up type whose youth and light weight may help in a sprint finish but overall profile is the weakest in the field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked seventh of eight on our figures, Last Flight makes a tough ask here; she has run over today's trip and returns after 19 days, but those are slim positives for a filly who has not threatened at this level.

runners_data.name: Make A Splash
runners_data.note: Lowest OR (45) in the field and flagged as a horse that fades in the finish, the worst possible profile for a race likely to be decided by a late sprint; weight advantage (114lbs) exists but the finishing tendency and modest form across four runs makes this an outsider in any shape.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, with a pair of eighth-place finishes sandwiching a sixth and a ninth, Make A Splash faces a stiff ask on these figures; she has run over today's trip and going before, and 19 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh.

races.paceDynamic: Sneaky Blinder is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner field over two miles at Ffos Las on Good turf, and with no rival capable of seriously pressuring them for the lead, they are likely to dictate at a measured, sustainable tempo from the outset. The remainder of the field is overwhelmingly hold-up in style, meaning the pace is unlikely to be severe enough to burn Sneaky Blinder off, and a controlled gallop from the front is the most probable race shape. This creates a scenario where the race is likely to be slowly run early before accelerating in the straight, compressing the field and making it harder for true hold-up horses to find daylight and generate meaningful momentum. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Merrijig, Beaune, Simiyann, Last Flight and Make A Splash are all true back-of-the-field horses who will find themselves bunched in a midfield cluster rather than getting clean separation. In this configuration, this race shape heavily favours the front-running or prominent profile and any hold-up horse with an exceptional turn of foot to navigate a messy closing stretch — but the dominant tactical verdict is that Sneaky Blinder dictating an uncontested lead is the standout structural advantage.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sneaky Blinder Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Sneaky Blinder is allowed to stride clear uncontested and sets a measured, undemanding pace through the first mile.
scenarios.body: Sneaky Blinder dictates every fraction, the pack behind is compressed into a bunch, and when the sprint begins in the straight the leader has energy reserves to repel challengers; this is the race shape that most rewards the horse controlling the tempo from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently in the final half-mile to stretch the field and allow a true finisher to pick off the leader.
scenarios.body: A horse tracking wide or angled wide in the home straight finds open ground and runs down the tiring leader with a sustained finish; this suits any hold-up horse that genuinely gets to race in their natural position rather than being boxed into a congested midfield.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough that a horse sitting second or third can time a challenge perfectly at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: A prominent racer conserves energy tracking the leader and produces a decisive move on the final bend, having enjoyed a clean trip throughout without the scrambling that afflicts the midfield pack; the compressed field actually benefits the horse closest to the leader.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Bunched Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that virtually the entire field arrives at the final furlong together.
scenarios.body: The race turns into a mass sprint and the outcome becomes chaotic and positional, with lighter-weighted or physically fresher horses potentially finding an advantage in the scramble; tactical luck and draw become more relevant than style.

watchPoints.text: Sneaky Blinder sets off in front with no rival able to press — watch whether Rossa Ryan chooses to dictate or is pushed wide, as their ability to get to the rail uncontested in the first furlong will define the entire race shape.

Golden Flame (Zoe Lewis, 7lbs claim) has the strongest Good-ground record in the field at this distance — if Lewis can position close enough to the leader from the back of the field to make one clean run, the form figures make this a credible threat to any front-runner.

Merrijig, Beaune, Simiyann, Last Flight and Make A Splash are all true hold-up horses forced to race in a congested midfield cluster — watch the closing stages for significant interference or horses unable to find gaps as the field bunches before the final furlong.

Lusaka carries the longest gap since last run (49 days) and hood headgear — if ring-rustiness shows early, this horse may be outpaced before getting into a rhythm, but if Flint has them tuned up the staying form on Good ground is genuinely competitive.

Last Flight (3yo, 120lbs) is the youngest and lightest runner — watch whether the low weight allows this horse to race closer than their natural style, effectively filling the prominent position that is otherwise only occupied by Sneaky Blinder.

races.name: Bni Elli Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Blue Hercules
runners_data.note: Trainer Muir & Grassick have shown OR=86 form over 10-12f on Good ground, placing twice from six similar-going runs; hold-up by nature but with several genuine closers in this field, it may find itself drawn closer to the pace than ideal, which tempers confidence in its finishing effort landing at the right moment.

runners_data.name: Pacific Storm
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's 69-day absence is worth noting for fitness, though Egan takes the ride and the horse has experience at this exact trip on Good — its two runs suggest it travels without issue but has yet to reach the frame; from its natural hold-up berth, it needs a strong enough gallop to close down a controlled front-runner.

runners_data.name: Phantom Recon
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-setter and the horse this entire race shape pivots around; George Scott's operation has sent out 2 winners from 26 runners in the past 14 days, and Keenan gets a golden opportunity to dictate terms uncontested — the slight style-fit flag means it isn't a natural leader, so watch for any early hesitation in the stalls.

runners_data.name: Winday
runners_data.note: Emmet Mullins runner with a hurdles background and all career runs on Heavier ground — the step up to Good turf here is a going question-mark, and the 89-day absence adds fitness doubt; stays long trips well in principle, having placed over 15f on Heavy, but the surface and style shift are material risks.

runners_data.name: Neswick
runners_data.note: Marcus Tregoning lightly raced type with just two runs on Tapeta at 10f — the switch to turf over 1m4f on Good is entirely untested; 14 days since last run keeps fitness ticking, and the unknown ceiling at this trip is the key variable — if the form from Kempton translates, Muscutt has the craft to place it prominently.

runners_data.name: Saaffya
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's debutant with Kieran Shoemark aboard — going UNKNOWN and no form to assess; Walker's stable runs at 2/41 in the last 14 days, so not in blazing form, but first-time starters from this yard with top jockeys at fair-ground maiden trips deserve respect and this one carries a high OR entry of 120.

races.paceDynamic: Phantom Recon is the sole confirmed front-runner in a six-horse field and should be able to dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo over 1m4f on Good turf at Ffos Las — a flat, undemanding track that suits a horse who can bowl along and use the bends efficiently. With no rival willing or able to seriously challenge for the lead, Phantom Recon sets a sustainable gallop that plays directly into the hands of horses who can track in behind and produce a clean, sustained run from two furlongs out rather than requiring a late, dramatic sprint. The hold-up horses — Blue Hercules, Pacific Storm, and Winday — sit deeper, but with only one true pace-setter likely to set a modest, measured tempo, the race may not truly come back to them in time, favouring prominent trackers over genuine closers. This race shape decisively favours horses racing in the second or third position, poised to pounce off a steady, uncontested lead — the prominent-to-midfield profile benefits most. The field carries more hold-up weight than the pace map can accommodate at the rear; Blue Hercules is the most likely of the redistributed types to be forced wider and closer to the pace than its natural style, though Pacific Storm's class could see it travelling handily despite its hold-up profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Phantom Recon Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Phantom Recon bowls along uncontested and sets a steady, measured pace that rewards close trackers.
scenarios.body: Phantom Recon dictates from the front on a flat, straightforward track and those travelling just behind in second or third can pounce when the tempo lifts at the two-furlong pole; closers left with genuine ground to make up may simply not get there in time on a track that doesn't stretch the field. Prominent and early-midfield profiles who travel smoothly within range of the pace are the primary beneficiaries here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closer Finishes Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to set things up for the hold-up horses to close off a strong run from two out.
scenarios.body: A steadier-than-expected early gallop can sometimes lull the pace-setter into accelerating too hard mid-race, creating a fast final two furlongs that favours horses with a high cruising speed arriving late; Pacific Storm's class and form experience at this trip makes it the most plausible closer to benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debutant Lands a Blow
scenarios.trigger: If Saaffya on debut shows natural ability and a settled travelling style that allows her to feature prominently throughout.
scenarios.body: Ed Walker debutants with Kieran Shoemark can often arrive well-prepared, and an unknown runner with a high OR and no going history could surprise on a fair, uncomplicated track if blessed with natural class and a comfortable racing style; the unknown quantity cuts both ways, but the team's strike-rate gives this scenario credibility.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Capitalises
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops chaotically — pace wavers, fancied horses travel poorly — allowing a lightly-regarded runner to scoop.
scenarios.body: With Winday carrying hurdles form and a wide market position, and Blue Hercules potentially racing out of its natural hold-up role closer to the pace, a scrambled finish could see an unexpected runner profit from positional chaos; this depends on multiple things going wrong for the principals simultaneously.

watchPoints.text: Watch Phantom Recon's early lead — if it goes unchallenged through the first half mile on a flat track, the race may effectively be won and lost by the time the field rounds the home turn; any drifting in price pre-race signals the market agrees.

Saaffya debuts for Ed Walker with Kieran Shoemark: debut runners from well-regarded trainers with booking of this calibre can be ready to go first time, and with going listed as UNKNOWN she is the biggest X-factor in the field — watch the market move closely.

Winday's switch from Heavy Irish hurdle tracks to Good flat turf at Ffos Las is a meaningful change of conditions; if it fails to handle the surface in the early stages and drops towards the rear, its chance is likely over given the controlled pace anticipated.

Pacific Storm's 69-day break means fitness is not guaranteed; watch how it travels in the first half of the race — if it looks laboured or is off the bridle early, the layoff may have dulled its sharpness despite David Menuisier's strong overall record.

Neswick's two Tapeta runs at Kempton provide limited surface-transfer data — watch how Daniel Muscutt positions it in the first quarter mile, as the jockey's placement choice will telegraph whether connections believe it handles the turf switch with confidence.

races.name: Ex1 Digital Forensic Services Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fast Steps
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old prominent racer with solid recent form at 12f on Good, going 12/15 on similar conditions; Charlie Tucker (7) takes the mount for Rod Millman, whose yard is ticking over at 2/19 in 14 days, and the visor adds focus — this horse's chief asset is slotting straight onto Takeitorleaveit's back and pressing at the right moment.
runners_data.comment: Fast Steps shaped with promise when runner-up three starts back and placed again four starts back, and our rating of 71 marks him out as a serious threat to the top-rated runner here; the worry is that he has been winless in his last five starts and dropped to fourth last time out.

runners_data.name: Symphony's Song
runners_data.note: Ian Williams filly stepping back up to 10f+ after two starts over shorter; her best form of 3/10f/GOO fits today's conditions well, and Ryan Kavanagh gives her experienced handling — she needs to improve on recent efforts but the trip and going combination is in her favour.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Symphony's Song has been placed twice recently but ranks eighth of nine on our figures, making her hard to fancy despite the experience over today's trip and going, and a return after just 18 days.

runners_data.name: Takeitorleaveit
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's 3-year-old is the race's sole confirmed front-runner with a remarkable 1W4P record on similar going; from stall position he should stride straight to the front uncontested, and Donagh Murphy (5) is capable of judging the pace — the only risk is if he fails to see out the trip having done all the work.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and a winner two starts back, Takeitorleaveit arrives 31 days fresh with experience over today's trip, though he carries 135 lb from stall 3 and his speed rating of 55 leaves him with something to prove against stronger company.

runners_data.name: Revich
runners_data.note: Adrian Wintle's veteran 10-year-old is a confirmed hold-up horse whose genuine rear-of-field style cannot be accommodated given how many closers are in this field; the visor suggests he needs to be scrubbed along, and 41 days off plus an OR of 58 makes it hard to see him getting competitive even from a midfield berth — his [STYLE_FIT] tag rightly tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Revich has shown consistent placing ability in recent starts, finishing third twice and fourth twice in his last six, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions — our rating of 71 suggests he merits plenty of respect at the weights. The concern is that he arrives 41 days fresh and remains winless in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Brave Leader
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's 3-year-old has finished no better than fourth in six starts, including twice at 11-12f, and the blinkers haven't unlocked anything yet; a hold-up racer with no wins and no places on similar going, he faces a stiff ask to improve here despite the claim of Liam Wright.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Brave Leader at least has experience of today's trip and going to call on, and 31 days between runs suggests he returns fresh; carrying 133 lb from stall eight, however, he faces a stiff task to improve on a sequence of mid-to-rear finishes.

runners_data.name: Sahm Naif
runners_data.note: Two wins from six runs on Good going over 10f make Sahm Naif one of the better-credentialed horses in the race for today's conditions; Alfie Redman (7) claims 7lbs which reduces his 132lbs burden meaningfully, and James Horton's yard is live at 1/4 in 14 days — the prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking Takeitorleaveit.

runners_data.name: Grand Pier
runners_data.note: Warren Greatrex's 3-year-old returns after 71 days off, a significant freshness flag, and his best result (2nd/10f/SOF) came on softer ground; Harry Vigors (3) claims, but this hold-up runner needs a stronger pace than Takeitorleaveit is likely to set to bring his finish into play.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Grand Pier nonetheless catches the eye as the top-rated runner in this field, and he has run over today's trip and going before; second last time out is the most compelling angle here, though 71 days off will need to be overcome.

runners_data.name: Tales Old As Time
runners_data.note: Edward Smyth-Osbourne's 3-year-old arrives on the back of weak form figures over shorter trips (8f/STA, 8f/HEA) and steps up markedly in trip to 10f; by nature a hold-up horse given his profile, he finds himself squeezed into a midfield role by the race's structural shape — the step up in trip is unproven and form does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: The Anthony Gover
runners_data.note: Charlie Bell (7) partners this 3-year-old for Dr Newland & Insole, who are quiet at 0/8 in 14 days; his best form of 3/10f/GOO is at least on-point for today, but six runs without a win and a propensity to fill midfield positions leave him reliant on a race developing in a way this pace map doesn't suggest is likely.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and showing a bit more spark than his previous efforts, The Anthony Gover has experience over today's trip and going, and at 131 lb from stall 5 he arrives fit on a 16-day turnaround with our rating suggesting he holds more ability than his official mark of 61 implies; the chief concern is his tendency to find a few too many rivals too strong.

runners_data.name: Hotel California
runners_data.note: David Menuisier's lightly-raced 3-year-old has only three career starts, all resulting in defeats, including an 8th over 8f on Standard — his natural hold-up style is compressed into midfield by field dynamics, he steps up to 10f for the first time, and Mason Paetel has very limited opportunities; the [STYLE_FIT] flag correctly signals he is unlikely to run his best race in this configuration.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Hotel California faces a stiff ask here; she has run over today's trip before and 31 days between runs suggests she arrives fresh, but a burden of 130 lb makes life harder still.

races.paceDynamic: Takeitorleaveit is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to dispute the lead, should slot onto the pace unchallenged from the outset over this 1m2f trip at Ffos Las on Good turf. From that uncontested position, Donagh Murphy (5) can dictate tempo in his own time, setting a sustainable gallop that plays directly to Takeitorleaveit's proven front-running style — this horse has finished first or second in seven of twelve starts on similar going. The prominent racers Fast Steps, Symphony's Song, and Sahm Naif will track just behind, giving them a clear sightline on the leader and the ability to pounce inside the final two furlongs without having to weave through traffic. This race shape strongly favours prominent and close-tracking runners, as a single uncontested front-runner on a flat track with a steady, controlled tempo gives the horse(s) immediately on its heels the ideal platform to strike — true hold-up horses who need a strong pace to close into will find conditions against them. Note that this field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can place at the rear: Tales Old As Time, Hotel California, and Revich are genuine hold-up horses redistributed to midfield on the map, but in practice Takeitorleaveit's controlled fractions will leave real closers with too little pace to chase down.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Takeitorleaveit Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit bowls along in front at a measured tempo and no prominent rival applies early pressure.
scenarios.body: Murphy settles the 3-year-old in an uncontested lead, controls fractions on a flat track, and kicks again when challenged — his 1W4P record on similar going underlines this is his optimum scenario. Prominent trackers who keep tabs on him throughout are the chief dangers as no significant late pace develops.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit's early lead is tracked closely by Fast Steps and Sahm Naif and one of them times a challenge to perfection turning for home.
scenarios.body: Sahm Naif arrives with two recent wins on Good going over 10f and sits comfortably just off the pace before pouncing, while Fast Steps's experience over this exact course configuration makes him a reliable each-way threat in this shape. Both horses race in role and need no redistribution, giving them a clean tactical advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Raider Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If Takeitorleaveit sets a stronger-than-expected tempo and the race develops into a proper test, giving a prominent-to-midfield runner a chance to run through.
scenarios.body: Symphony's Song has shown her best form over 10f on Good ground and could creep into contention from just off the pace if the fractions quicken; The Anthony Gover also holds some form on Good going over 10f and could benefit if the pace serves runners coming from slightly further back. However, this scenario depends on Takeitorleaveit going too fast for his own good, which his tactical profile suggests is unlikely.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a true hold-up horse manages to finish strongly from off the bridle.
scenarios.body: This shape requires genuine end-to-end froth that the pace map explicitly rules out — Revich, Tales Old As Time, and Hotel California are all true hold-up types but are physically redistributed into midfield on this map, and their [STYLE_FIT] tags confirm they are unlikely to get the deep closing run they need. Grand Pier or Brave Leader, neither of whom has shown the form to win off a slow pace, represent slim alternatives but lack the RPR profile to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Takeitorleaveit jumping cleanly and reaching the lead without interference is the single most important moment of this race — if he is bumped or slow away, the entire pace structure collapses and the shape becomes unpredictable.

Sahm Naif and Fast Steps tracking Takeitorleaveit closely from the outset — if both press him rather than sitting quietly, they could compromise his rhythm and inadvertently drag up the tempo, creating a stronger pace than expected and a marginally more open finish.

Grand Pier returns after 71 days off with no recent racecourse evidence; watch for signs of a big run first time back, as fresh horses at Ffos Las over this trip on Good ground can show up unexpectedly if the trainer has them ready.

The three redistributed hold-up horses — Tales Old As Time, Hotel California, and Revich — are worth watching in the early stages: if any of them push forward to find their natural rhythm, they will crowd the midfield and potentially disrupt Symphony's Song or The Anthony Gover's race.

Jockey bookings with claims (Tucker 7, Redman 7, Bell 7, Vigors 3, Murphy 5) affect actual weights significantly across this field — monitor declared weights at the off as several runners are at the margin where the claim is the difference between a competitive and overweight burden.
